title: Data Center Gas Plants to Boost US Power Emissions by 20%
source_used: Bloomberg News analysis via Fortune (18 Aug 2026)
key_facts: Bloomberg analysis of BloombergNEF data: 99 proposed on-site gas plants for data centers.
They would emit about 318 million metric tons of CO2 a year at industry-standard rates, against about 1,485 million tons for the whole US power industry last year.
That could lift US power-sector emissions by 20%, and as much as a third if plants ran flat out.
Based on 126 GW of planned on-site gas generation; projects in 22 states, more than a third in Texas.
Not all plants are likely to be built; some are phantom projects or long shots.
quote_evidence: Ninety-nine proposed plants tracked by BloombergNEF would emit about 318 million metric tons of carbon dioxide annually if run at industry-standard rates, according to a Bloomberg News analysis.
Not all of the proposed plants in the BNEF data are likely to be built.
why_it_matters_hint: Gas built for data centers could make Big Tech's climate goals harder to meet.
